questions.question: When is the product $AB$ defined?
options: When $A$ and $B$ have the same size.
When the columns of $A$ match the rows of $B$
Only when $A$ has more rows than $B$.
Only when both matrices are diagonal

questions.question: If $A$ is $m\times n$ and $B$ is $n\times k$, what is the size of $AB$?
What does the entry $(AB)_{ij}$ combine?
options: The sizes of $A$ and $B$ but not their entries.
Only the diagonal entries of $A$ and $B$.

questions.question: What does matrix product represent for linear maps?
options: The determinant of a rectangular matrix.
The kernel of a map only.

questions.question: Is matrix multiplication generally commutative?
options: Yes, whenever both products are defined.
No; order can change or prevent the product.
Yes, if the entries are real numbers.

questions.question: A $2\times3$ matrix is multiplied by a $3\times4$ matrix. What is the size of the product?
Compute $\begin{pmatrix}1&2\\0&1\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}3\\4\end{pmatrix}$.
Which product is defined?
If $A$ is $4\times1$ and $B$ is $1\times6$, what is the size of $AB$?
For $A=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\2&1\end{pmatrix}$ and $B=\begin{pmatrix}3&4\\5&6\end{pmatrix}$, what is the $(2,1)$ entry of $AB$?
Why can $AB$ be defined while $BA$ is not?
options: If one order is defined, the other is always defined.
The entries of $A$ must all be larger than those of $B$.
The inner dimensions are checked separately for the two orders.

questions.question: What does associativity of matrix multiplication allow you to do?
options: Replace every product by an entrywise product
Regroup a product like $(AB)C$ as $A(BC)$ when defined

questions.question: Why is matrix multiplication defined by row-column products rather than entrywise?
options: It exists only to compute determinants.
It ignores rows and columns completely.
It matches composition of linear maps.
It is defined only for matrices with one entry.

questions.question: Let $A$ be $2\times3$, $B$ be $3\times2$, and $C$ be $2\times5$. Which product is defined?
Compute the top-left entry of $\begin{pmatrix}1&2\\3&4\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}0&5\\1&6\end{pmatrix}$.
If $A$ is $2\times3$ and $AB$ is $2\times4$, what size can $B$ have?
Why does the formula $(AB)_{ij}=\sum_{r=1}^n a_{ir}b_{rj}$ use a summation index $r$?
options: It labels the diagonal entries only.
It forces the product to be commutative.
It counts the number of rows of the product
It pairs a row of $A$ with a column of $B$

questions.question: Can two nonzero matrices have a zero product?
options: Only if both matrices are identity matrices.
Only if the matrices are not compatible for multiplication.
Yes, matrix multiplication can have zero divisors.
Only if one matrix is a zero matrix.

questions.question: Give the product $AB$ for $A=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&1\end{pmatrix}$ and $B=\begin{pmatrix}1&-1\\-1&1\end{pmatrix}$.
Let $A$ be $3\times2$ and $B$ be $2\times3$. Which statement about $AB$ and $BA$ is correct?
options: Both are undefined because the matrices are not square.
Both are defined, but $AB$ is $3\times3$ and $BA$ is $2\times2$.
Both are defined and must have the same size.
